IMPLEMENTER_REPORT:
ROUND: 0
STATUS: DONE

SELF_REVIEW:
- TDD evidence: RED first. Added `generate_manifest_derives_failure_from_skill_files` (crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs) and `entry_failure_reasons_keep_their_wording_on_the_skill_file`. Before the implementation `cargo test -p skill-index` failed only on the manifest test: "assertion `left == right` failed: a failed entry must not invent a manifest entry / left: [\"gated\", \"open\"] / right: [\"open\"]" (a directory that exists but lacks its root SKILL.md was not skipped, because `generate_manifest` consulted the directory-level status). After the implementation both tests pass.
- AC1 (entry no longer exposes directory-level status; failure derived from skill files): removed `pub resolution: ResolutionStatus` from `ExpectedSetEntry` and every construction site (`discover_skills`, `resolved_entry`, `failed_entry`, test `entry()` helper, synthetic manifest test literal). `failed_entry` keeps the reason on the root `SkillFile` only. `generate_manifest` now uses `skill.is_failed()` — failure is derived from the skill files the entry owns (ADR-0045).
- AC2 (messages keep naming the missing location and reason): new `entry_failure_reasons_keep_their_wording_on_the_skill_file` pins the exact previous strings on the root skill file: "vendor skill directory not found: <abs path>", "upstream skill directory not found: <path>", and `malformed skillPath "<path>": expected a path ending in /SKILL.md`. The existing missing-vendor / missing-upstream enumerator tests were migrated to the root skill file and still require the reason class plus the missing path. Packaging (`reject_failed_entries` formats `'name' (source skill, file): reason`) and validation matrix wording tests were untouched and stay green.
- AC3 (compiles, workspace tests green, no reader of the retired status, clippy clean): `cargo test --workspace` passes; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes; grep confirms no `entry.resolution` / `skill.resolution` reads — the only `.resolution` reads are on `SkillFile` (`file.resolution`, `skill_file(..).resolution`).
- AC4 (behavior unchanged): dev policy, pack strictness, tarball/installed layout, lock format, and all five entry-state verdicts are unchanged; the existing referee suites pass. Deliberate changes, both required by ADR-0045: (a) the entry-level `resolution` field and its reason strings leave the `ExpectedSetEntry` interface; (b) `generate_manifest` derives failure from skill files, which closes the latent #118 path where a present directory with a missing root SKILL.md could still invent a manifest entry (the shipped pack flow is unchanged because packaging rejects failed entries before generating the manifest). `ResolutionStatus` itself stays as the Skill-file state; the reason vocabulary moved onto the file. CONTEXT.md's **Expected-set entry** definition and the `ResolutionStatus` docs were updated to match.
- AC5 (no assertion relaxed): the touched enumerator assertions were migrated, not weakened (`assert_eq!(entry.resolution, Resolved)` became `assert!(!entry.is_failed(), ...)` plus root-skill-file checks; failure tests now require the reason class and missing path instead of only a name fragment). No existing assertion was deleted or loosened.
- Regression evidence: final `cargo test --workspace` exit 0, every suite ok (35, 113, 3, 8, 15, 9, 17, 1, 4, 1, 4, 17, 24, 23, 28, 34, plus doc-tests; only pre-existing `unused dependency anyhow/serde_json` warnings in crates/validation/Cargo.toml). Note: one intermediate full run hit a pre-existing flake outside this change — `crates/distill-cli` `transition::tests::commit_writes_run_artifact_with_exact_bytes` raced its sibling `events_are_appended_before_state_is_written`, which exports the process-global `DISTILL_FAIL_WRITE_STATE_FOR_RUN=run-1` while tests share a process (crates/distill-cli/src/transition.rs:272-281); the immediate rerun was green and distill-cli is untouched by this diff. `bash scripts/sandboxed-rust-script.sh --test tests/test_install.rs` 7 passed; `bash scripts/sandboxed-rust-script.sh --test tests/test_toolkit_setup.rs` 1 passed. `cargo fmt -p skill-index -- --check` and `cargo fmt -p validation-runner -- --check` are clean (the repo has pre-existing rustfmt drift in unrelated crates; those files were not touched). No scope creep: no type renames, no doc rewrites beyond the affected terms, no test files edited.
CHANGED_FILES:
- crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs (removed `ExpectedSetEntry::resolution` and its construction sites; `generate_manifest` derives failure via `is_failed()`; `ResolutionStatus`/`SkillFile` docs updated; enumerator tests migrated and two new tests added)
- crates/validation-runner/src/lib.rs (test helper no longer sets the retired field; failure-section and matrix-case comments updated)
- CONTEXT.md (Expected-set entry definition now names the Skill files the entry owns)
- crates/deploy/src/dev.rs (pre-existing) — already derives skip/warning from skill files
- crates/deploy/src/pack.rs (pre-existing) — already rejects and names every missing skill file
- tests/test_install.rs (pre-existing) — dev/pack referee suite
- tests/test_toolkit_setup.rs (pre-existing) — reads `is_failed()` / `file.resolution`
- docs/adr/0045-expected-set-entry-resolves-its-skill-files.md (pre-existing) — decision this ticket completes
- corpus/issue-121.json (pre-existing) — parent spec
- corpus/issue-126.json (pre-existing) — this ticket
SUMMARY: Retired the entry-level resolution status: `ExpectedSetEntry` no longer carries a directory-level verdict, `generate_manifest` derives failure from the skill files the entry owns, and all dev/pack/validation messages, verdicts, and layouts keep their previous wording and behavior.
